injection: ## 2. Identity and scoped-mutation injection (120 test sources)

Every source sentence of data/items/test.jsonl was given to the production judge as if it were the `full`-channel output for its own source (input `The user typed: <source>`), then scored by the unchanged src/attribute.py (J1/J2, layer0 tiebreak for general dims, arbiter for critical J1!=J2). One hand-written, scoped mutation per source (analysis/oracle/source_mutations.jsonl, frozen before judging) flips the critical value and is scored against the *unmutated* source's contract. 17/120 mutations coincide with the family's partner source (minimal pairs admit few other scoped flips); the rest are new wordings.
Critical J1!=J2 disagreements: identity 1/120, mutants 1/120; these went to the arbiter (critical_source=arbiter).

challenges: ## 3. Challenge items (24 round-1 + 48 new)

The 48 new sentences (annotation/challenge_items_r2.jsonl) were written by hand, without LLM help, with keys frozen before any judge call (sha256 in analysis/oracle/challenge_keys_frozen.sha256). Each control is a valid instance of its contract value. Each mutant changes one feature of its paired control and is scored against the *control's* contract value. A control fails (false alarm) when the production critical_match rejects it. A mutant is detected when critical_match rejects it. `raw` is the same rule without the D-015 acceptance~statement relaxation.
| group | false alarms (prod) | mutants detected (prod) | false alarms (raw) | mutants detected (raw) | critical label = key | keyed general labels correct | J1!=J2 |

**Gate (PREREG_R2: mutants detected >= 22/24, false alarms <= 1/24):** production oracle 22/24 detected, 0/24 false alarms -> **PASS**. Raw oracle 24/24, 0/24 -> **PASS**. The prereg says '22/24 per new group' but each group has only 6 mutants and 6 controls, so I read the gate as pooled over the 24 new mutants and 24 new controls. Per-group counts are in the table; no group can be certified with n=6 (a 6/6 Wilson lower bound is 0.61).

Per-group strict reading (all 6 mutants detected and 0 false alarms): acceptance 4/6 det, 0/6 FA -> not met, embedded_actor 6/6 det, 0/6 FA -> ok, mitigation 6/6 det, 0/6 FA -> ok, question_request 6/6 det, 0/6 FA -> ok.

panel: ## 4. Codex annotator panel vs the production judge (main1 gold, 163 sampled + 24 round-1 challenges)

Panel: C-gpt-5.6-sol, C-gpt-6-astra, C-gpt-6-luna (machine annotators; none is the judge gpt-6.1-sol or the tested gpt-6.1-terra). **This is machine-machine agreement, not human validation. The PREREG kappa>=0.6 gate applies to human gold only, and no human returns exist yet (annotation/returns/ is absent).** Production labels: J1==J2, else the arbiter (13 sampled critical labels were null in gold_key_main1.csv and are now filled from runs/main1/arbiter.jsonl), general dims use the layer0 tiebreak. Labels the panel member listed in `unsure_dims` are treated as missing, which matches the annotate.html export. Majority means at least 2 of 3 members, and more than half of the non-missing votes. Design weights are 1/pi from gold_key_main1.csv (Horvitz-Thompson); weighted CIs use the Kish effective n. Challenge items have no pi and are scored unweighted, in a separate subset.

Data notes: {"out_of_schema:politeness=plain": 2, "out_of_schema:speech_act=acceptance": 3, "rows_with_extra_columns": 43, "unsure:added_content": 10, "unsure:agent": 19, "unsure:certainty": 7, "unsure:critical": 3, "unsure:polarity": 3, "unsure:politeness": 2, "unsure:speech_act": 15}. The 43 rows with an extra column are all of C_gpt-6-luna_extraB.csv, which has one surplus empty field after added_content. The label columns parse correctly. Out-of-schema general labels are kept as given (speech_act=acceptance, politeness=plain) and count as disagreements.

verdicts: Each sampled gold unit (text, family, visible input) maps to one or more scored occurrences in runs/main1/scored.parquet: different variants share bare/noncrit inputs, and models and prompts can produce the same text. For every occurrence I recomputed Violation (cue channels), Assumption (bare/noncrit) and constraint_preserving (cue channels) twice. The first run used the production judge labels; recomputing them reproduces the stored production verdicts exactly ({'ok': 1041}). The second run used panel-majority labels for the critical and general dims. A verdict *flips* when the two runs give different non-missing values. When the panel has no majority on a needed label, that verdict is unresolved, not a flip. Production semantics ignore a missing general label; the `strict` columns in the CSV treat it as unresolved instead.
